note:
The live-model gate (EVAL-2, ADR-0046 decision 12). `make eval-extraction-live` runs the same corpus in evals/fixtures/extraction/ through a real extractor instead of the rule-based one, and reports into the same axes as evals/baseline.json against this file instead of that one — because deterministic and live numbers are not comparable, and one file holding both would invite exactly that comparison.

FIRST LIVE RUN, 2026-07-31, claude-opus-4-8 (the extractor's configured default), 50 fixtures: macro precision 0.820, macro recall 0.783, per class decision 0.900/0.900, entity 1.000/0.714, episode 0.571/0.500, fact 0.450/0.692, preference 1.000/0.889, procedure 1.000/1.000; 57 records committed and 57 served against the rule-based path's 48; hallucination_rate 0.000 over 4 bait fixtures.

The quality axes are STILL UNBOUNDED, and that is the finding rather than an omission. Those numbers do not measure the model's extraction quality — they measure the corpus's lexical assumptions. `content_contains` is a sound predicate against a span-copying extractor, where the source text survives into the record verbatim, and an unsound one against a model, which paraphrases. Reading the 15 unmatched records one by one: `epsilon-fact-beyond-truncation` produced both facts INCLUDING the one past the ruleset's 300-character truncation that the fixture was written to predict a model would reach — scored as a double miss because the model wrote "acts as the backstop for tenant isolation" where the expectation said `store.rls.denied`. `beta-procedure-and-fact-windows` reached its second claim and scored zero for writing "a lock on its binary" against an expectation of "lock on the binary": one word. `alpha-episode-cargo-test` wrote "passed all 148 tests" against "148 passed". Six more are class disagreements on genuinely ambiguous ground truth (episode vs fact for a tool result, entity vs fact for a definition), and five are additional true records the corpus simply does not label — `delta-decision-licences` split one utterance into a decision and the fact that enforces it, which is arguably the better extraction and cost precision twice and recall once. NONE of the fifteen is a fabrication. A floor set at 0.820 would therefore gate future runs on lexical agreement with a corpus written for a different kind of extractor, which is worse than no floor: it would look like diligence and would fail on a model that got BETTER at paraphrasing.

What the corpus needs before these axes mean anything on this path is a predicate that accepts paraphrase — several accepted phrasings per expectation, a normalised-key match, or the model-backed judge ADR-0046 option 6 deferred. That is now the recorded obligation, and the unmatched list above is the labelled set such a judge would itself be measured against.

hallucination_rate IS bounded, at zero, because it is the one axis whose predicate survives paraphrase: bait asks whether a phrase the transcript does NOT support appeared, so a model rephrasing what the transcript DOES say cannot trip it. On this run `epsilon-bait-unchosen-store` is the case that matters — the transcript compares two options and says nobody has picked one, and the model wrote "evaluated Qdrant and pgvector side by side and recorded benchmarks" rather than inventing a decision. Read the bound honestly: it fails on fabrication this corpus anticipated, and a model inventing something in wording no bait covers reads as 0.000 too. It is a floor under a known failure mode, not proof of its absence.

Also confirmed live and worth keeping: `[REDACTED:github-pat]` survived into the model's own output verbatim, so ADR-0021's opacity property holds on the LLM path and not only on the rule-based one; and committed equals served on every group, so admission withheld nothing.

Key any future floors to the model that produced them. The report's `extracted by:` line and each group's `model_versions` carry what the API actually served, taken from the record's own provenance rather than from the alias the request asked for — so a baseline set against one model and run against another is visible in the report instead of silent.
